 (SCCH3) 3 MVC.No.380/2021  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ for the death of Master Tarun R in the road traffic accident occurred on 31.08.2017.
02.

The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that on 31.08.2017 when the deceased namely Tarun R was standing in front of landlord Mudlagiraiah's building, a tanker Tractor bearing No.KA 41T252 which came to fill water from borewell and its driver took reverse in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
Due to this the said Tarun R sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Then he was taken to Sri Lakshmi hospital, Bengaluru, but on the way itself he had succumbed due to fatal injuries.
Thereafter the dead body was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical College & hospital, Bengaluru and postmortem was conducted and handed over the dead body to the petitioners.
Then the petitioners have shifted the dead body and conducted funeral and final rites by spending Rs.1,00,000/.

The deceased prior to the (SCCH3) 4 MVC.No.380/2021 accident was hale and healthy and was studying in IX standard and he was very sharp student and very active in extra curricular activities and had bright future.
Due to death of deceased the petitioners are suffering from loss of love and affection, loss of future dependency and mental agony.
The accident is due to the rash and negligent driving of tractor driver.
Hence the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and only respondent No.1 have filed written statement.
04. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 is as under: The petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
The tanker/trailer which is mentioned in the police records and attached to the tractor which dashed to the deceased and caused accident was not insured with this respondent.
The driver of the tractor is also necessary party to the proceedings.
This respondent has issued the policy to the tractor in the name of respondent No.2 which covers the date of (SCCH3) 5 MVC.No.380/2021 accident.
But the liability is subject to terms and conditions of policy.
The tractor driver was not holding valid driving licence.
Even the said tractor was ply on public road without Sri.Ramesh vs Iffco Tokio Genl.

Ins on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57875939/
2 registration and hence the respondent No.2 has violated the terms of the policy.
The said tractor has no permit on the date of accident.

The tractor driver had caused the accident with his rash and negligent driving and also without holding permit, D.L and fitness certificate and hence this respondent is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
This respondent denied the manner of accident, age of the deceased.
It is denied that the petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral ceremony.
The petitioners are put to strict proof of the same.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
05. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and got marked 09 documents as Ex.P.1 to 9 and closed their side.
06. By way of rebuttal, the Assistant Manager of the respondent No.1 and the SDA, RTO were got examined as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed their side.
Due to oversight the Ex.R.1 was marked as twice.
Heard arguments from both sides.
08. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:  ISSUES

1. Whether the petitioners proves that the deceased namely Tarun R when standing in front of Mudlagiraiah's building, at that time a tanker Tractor bearing No. KA41T252 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, due to this he had sustained grievous injuries and succumb to injuries at the hospital as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of Tarun R?
3. Whether the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties?

4. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the tractor driver did not hold valid driving licence,
permit and registration certificate on the date of accident and hence they are not liable to pay compensation?
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount & from whom?
6.
What order
or award?
09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In partly affirmative Issue No.3 In affirmative Issue No.4
In affirmative Issue No.5
In partly affirmative Issue No.6

As per final order for the following:
Sri.Ramesh vs Iffco Tokio Genl.
Ins on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57875939/
3 REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2:
These points will be taken at one stretch for my consideration in order to avoid repetition of facts as they are inter related with each other.
11. It is the grievance of the petitioners that the deceased Tarun R died in road traffic accident which took place on 31.08.2017 due to the rash and negligent driving of tractor driver.
Further they have (SCCH3) 8 MVC.No.380/2021 contended that they being the parents and sister of the deceased are suffering from loss of love and affection and loss of future dependency.
Hence, they have claimed compensation before this court.

12. Per contra, the same was denied by respondent No.1 and stated that the accident did not took place due to rash and negligent driving of tractor driver and hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.
13. In order to prove this, the petitioner No.1 was got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his crossexamination admitted that "That I am working at garments and getting Rs.12,000/ per month.
That my wife is not working anywhere.
I had lodged complaint to the police.
It is true that the police after investigation have filed chargesheet which is correct.
That I have seen the accident from far place.
That my son was standing on the way where tractor was coming.
That my son was standing on the edge of road.
That the said Mudlaiah was loading water daily in the said tractor tanker.
It is true that whenever the said tractor loaded with water usually took reverse side towards my house.
It is true that I have not seen (SCCH 3) 9 MVC.No.380/2021 whether the accident was caused by tractor or trailer.
It is true that this accident took place due to tractor tanker came from reverse side.
It is true that the backside of the tanker dashed to the deceased and it ran over on the deceased".
He had deposed based on the available documents on record and he had seen the accident from far place.
14. Per contra, the Assistant Manager of the respondent No.1 was got examined himself as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in his affidavit.
It is pertinent to note due to oversight the Ex.R.1 was marked as twice.
The RW.1 has got marked the copy of policy which is valid as on the date of accident which is only for tractor.
Hence the RW.1 has stated that they are not liable to pay compensation as they have not issued the policy to the trailer which had caused the accident.
15. The RW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "I do not know that difference between the tractor, tanker and trailer.
That the vehicle bearing registration No.KA41T252 is an tractor.
It is true that the tanker and the trailer are attached to the tractor.
It is true that we have issued policy only to the (SCCH3) 10 MVC.No.380/2021 tractor.

It is true that the said tractor had third party insurance".
16.
But there are no documents on behalf of the respondents to show that the accident did not took place.
So on basis of oral evidence of PW.1 and RW.1, it is clear that the accident took place and the deceased succumbed to the accidental injuries only.

sentences.text: Further the Pw.1 has got marked Ex.P.1 to 6 and 9 the police documents.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 to 6 and 9 the concerned I.O after investigation have filed Charge sheet against the tractor driver and owner for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and U/s 134(A & B), 187, 181, 192,
196 of IMV Act.
As per Ex.P.9 the concerned I.O has stated that the deceased died only due to the rash and negligent driving of tractor and trailer driver.
It is also stated that the said tractor and trailer was not having valid permit, registration and the driver was not having valid driving licence to drive the tractor.
18. Further the allegation of the petitioners are well supported with the mahazars marked at Ex.P.3 and 6.
As per Ex.P.3 and 6 the tractor and trailer driver due to his rash and negligent driving had dashed to the deceased.
As per Ex.P.6 the tractor and (SCCH3) 11 MVC.No.380/2021 trailer was seized by the concerned I.O.
Even as per Ex.P.5 the IMV report the said tractor and trailer had no fresh visible damages.
So, it is clear that the respondents have not proved that the accident did not took place and there is negligence on part of deceased to the accident.
Hence it is clear that the accident occurred due to the negligence of tractor and trailer driver only.
19. The respondents have not established that there is contributory negligence on part of deceased.
So simply stating negligence on part of deceased is not enough to accept the version of the respondents.
There is no supportive oral and documentary evidence on behalf of the respondents to show the negligence of the deceased for the accident.
20. Hence the respondents have not proved the negligence of the deceased for the accident.
Further the petitioners in order to prove that they are the parents and sister and legal heirs of the deceased have produced and marked the markscard of the deceased as per Ex.P.7.
So, basis of these documents, I am of opinion that the petitioners No.1
and 2 can be considered as the dependents and legal heirs of deceased
. The petitioner No.3 who is the sister and (SCCH3) 12 MVC.No.380/2021 minor cannot be considered as the legal heir of the deceased.
The petitioner No.3 is under the care and custody of her parents.
Hence only the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the parents can be considered as legal heir and dependents of the deceased.
Even the respondent No.2 had not challenged the Charge sheet filed against the tractor and trailer driver.
Hence I answered the issue No.1 in affirmative and issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
The respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties as the insurer and insured of the trailer were not made as parties.
It is true with the available documents that the back side of the tractor i.e trailer has caused the accident.
The said trailer is an seperate vehicle which is attached to the tractor.
The said trailer is not insured with any insurance company.
Hence as rightly contended that even the owner of the said trailer was not made as party.
Hence the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary party.
Hence I answered the issue No.3 in affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:

The respondent No.1 has contended that the tractor driver did not hold driving (SCCH3) 13 MVC.No.380/2021 licence, permit and registration certificate as on the date of accident and hence they are not liable to pay the compensation.
In this regard the respondent No.1 have got examined the SDA, RTO as RW.2 who had stated that the tractor bearing No.KA41T Sri.Ramesh vs Iffco Tokio Genl.

Ins on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57875939/
5 252 is meant for agricultural purpose.
That in their RTO the tractor is only registered and not trailer.
When the said vehicle is used for agricultural purpose there is no need of permit but if it is used for commercial activities then permit is required.

The RW.2 had got marked the letter as per Ex.R.1 again and Ex.R.2.
23.
So it is clear that at the time of accident the tractor was used for filling water which is a commercial activity.
So in order to do this work the permit is necessary.
The said owner of the tractor had not obtained permit as required under law.
Hence it is clear violation of the terms of the policy.
24. Further it is also clear that the accident was caused by the back side of the tractor which is the trailer.
The said trailer is not insured by any insurance company.
The tractor and trailer are both seperate vehicles.
Hence in view of not registering the said trailer and attached the tractor does not itself indemnify the insurance company as the tractor was (SCCH3) 14 MVC.No.380/2021 insured.
Hence the R.C owner of the tractor without validly registering the trailer and attached to the tractor has violated the terms of the policy.
25. Further it is true that the said trailer which is used and attached with the tractor was not validly insured with any insurance company.
Hence as the accident was caused by the trailer but the tractor driver the policy for the tractor is not covered for the tractor.
26. Even it is clear that as on the date of accident the said tractor and trailer driver had no valid driving licence.
As per settled principle of law merely not having driving licence is not a ground to exonerate the liability cast on the insurance company.
The principle of pay and recover is applicable to such cases.
But in the instant case as there is no permit and registration, the R.C owner cannot shift the liability on the insurance company.
Hence I answered the issue No.4 in affirmative.
27. Issue No.5:
In this case the petitioners have produced the markscard as per Ex.P.7 in which the date of birth of the deceased is not mentioned.
Hence under these circumstances it is just and proper to rely upon the police records.
Hence in Post mortem (SCCH3) 15 MVC.No.380/2021 report as per Ex.P.4 it is mentioned that deceased was 14 years old boy.

6 Rs.30,000/
by (SCCH3) 16 MVC.No.380/2021 applying proper multiplier of "15".
If multiplier of 15 is adopted, then it comes to Rs.30,000 x 15 = Rs.4,50,000/.
So, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for loss of dependency of Rs.4,50,000/ (Four lakhs fifty thousand only).
29. Further Rs.50,000/ (Fifty thousand only) has to be awarded under conventional heads as awarded in the said Judgment.
The petitioner No.3 is a minor sister of the deceased who is under care and custody of her parents are not entitled for compensation for the death of her brother in the road traffic accident.
Therefore, considering the same in my opinion the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ (Five lakhs only).
30. Regarding liability: The petitioners have proved that deceased sustained injuries only due to the rash and negligent manner of tractor and trailer driver.
The said tractor even though insured with the respondent No.1 but the trailer was not insured validly as on the date of accident 31.

At this stage the respondent No.1 has relied upon decisions reported in (SCCH3) 17 MVC.No.380/2021 a. 1997 ACJ 512 - The Oriental Insurance Company Limited V/s N.Chandrasheran - It is observed that the trailer is constructed for the purpose of carriage and goods vehicle and when it is pulled by a tractor both together constitute a transport vehicle.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited V/s N.Chandrasheran
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The trailer are covered under commercial vehicle type.

b. MFA No.30900/2010 - National Inurance Company Limited Vs Chandramma and others  It is observed that when the tractor is insured and trailer not insured and in absence of such provision under section 149(2) of the Act the court has no power to direct the insurer to pay and recover against a third party.

entities.text: MFA No.30900/2010 - National Inurance Company Limited Vs Chandramma and others
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: c. SLP.No.33638/17 - Balu Krishna Chavan Vs The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd., and others

entities.text: Balu Krishna Chavan Vs The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that in all cases pay and recover would not arise when there is no liability.
32. Hence the aforesaid preposition of law is aptly applicable to the facts of this case.

Hence it is clear that eventhough the tractor was duly insured with the respondent No.1 as on the date of accident, but the respondent No.1 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 for the reason that the said trailer was not duly insured, has no permit and registration.
(SCCH3) 18 MVC.No.380/2021
Even the principle of pay and recover is not applicable to the facts of this case eventhough the tractor driver had no valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence the R.C owner of the tractor eventhough insured the tractor has violated the terms of the policy by using the trailer without policy and for commercial activities.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the tractor is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 for the reason that the trailer which caused the accident was not insured with them.

Hence the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners No.1 and 2 for the reason that the trailer was used for commercial activity and ply on public road without having driving licence, permit, policy and registration.
Sri.Ramesh vs Iffco Tokio Genl.

Ins on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57875939/
7 33.
With regard to apportionment, the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased are entitled for 50% each of the amount awarded.
Hence, issue No.5 is answered in partly affirmative.
34. Issue No.6:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 5 as above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per (SCCH3) 19 MVC.No.380/2021 annum from the date of petition till deposit.

As such I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec 166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for Rs.5,00,000/ (Five lakhs only) as compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is alone liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner No.1 and 2 and shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
The claim of the petitioner No.3 is dismissed on without costs.
The claim against the respondent No.1 is dismissed on without costs.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the entire amount equally of the amount awarded and the Office is directed to release the entire amount to them (SCCH3) 20 MVC.No.380/2021 through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
